title: Token Prefill Merge and ASCII Fastpath
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a short-window coalescer for prefill tokenization that groups closely-timed compatible requests, routes merged work to SIMD/vectorized normalization kernels, and leverages a session-scoped prefix cache and ASCII fastpath to reduce CPU and per-request overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated behind 'prefill.coalescer_v1' with default off for hosted tier
E2E tests in CI showing tokenization correctness identical to non-coalesced path
Perf dashboards demonstrate >=20% CPU reduction for small-prompt workloads and >=1.5x throughput improvement for 1-32 token prefills in canary
Canary shows no >5ms increase in p99 prefill latency for production traffic
Coalescer auto-disables when predicted added latency >10ms or when request sets low-latency flag
implementation_notes: Ingress buffer: configurable coalescing window (default 6ms) implemented in tokenizer ingress layer
Compatibility gating: coalesce when session_id matches OR prefix similarity >0.8 using Jaccard on subtokens
Annotation: mark coalesced tasks with 'coalesced_prefill' for kernel selector to prefer SIMD-friendly kernels and adjusted microbatch sizes
Session cache: LRU prefix cache with 30m TTL; use hedged reads to reduce tail latency from cache node flaps
ASCII fastpath: apply vectorized ASCII normalization for coalesced batches and short-circuit heavy Unicode paths
Fallback heuristics: bypass coalescer when queue length >8, incoming rate spike, or request has strict latency requirement
Observability: emit coalesce_rate, avg_coalesce_size, predicted_saved_tokens, p99_added_latency, kernel_choice_post_coalesce
Correctness: property tests to ensure identical token outputs and preserved per-session ordering
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Created after cluster perf regression investigation on small prompt traffic; drafted design
2025-11-18: Spike prototype in local branch; synthetic benchmarks show ~30% CPU reduction when coalescing 2-4 concurrent prefills
2025-11-25: Runtime and Kernel teams reviewed design; agreed on kernel annotation contract and ASCII fastpath behavior
2025-11-28: Fixed concurrent cache write races via compare-and-swap; added integration tests for cache eviction semantics
2025-12-01: Feature flag and canary plan implemented; PRs opened for ingest and runtime routing
test_plan: Unit: tokenization equivalence tests for 2000 randomized prompts comparing coalesced vs independent runs
Property: session-order invariants and idempotency across retries
Integration: CI end-to-end correctness and latency tests using canary harness
Perf: microbench suite and canary workload for small prompt high-concurrency scenarios
Chaos: simulate cache node failures to validate hedged reads and tail latency mitigation
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal staging enablement; full perf and correctness sweep
Stage 2: Canary at 1% hosted traffic for 48 hours; monitor coalesce metrics and p99 prefill latency
Stage 3: Ramp to 20% over 24 hours if canary stable; verify CPU, throughput, and decode correctness
Stage 4: Global enable with automatic rollback if p99 added latency >5ms or error rate increase >0.05%
risks: Misconfigured window increases tail latency for single-request cases
Similarity heuristic false positives could merge unrelated requests affecting correctness and billing
Cache TTL tuning trade-offs between memory and hit rate
Kernel annotation mismatch may route coalesced work to suboptimal kernels and lose benefits
